note: Set A captures more of the page's real engineering content — the glass tile identity (FIRECLAY CRUSH "DANDELION", 2"x6"), the edge strip, the backsplash adhesive, and the D3 and D5 scales — while Set B drops all of these and instead pads with revision-history rows (admin, neutral) plus several invented conditions. Set B also misbinds the PT1 paint/finish code as a "PT1 substrate" and attaches an unsupported "Laundry Millwork Detail D5" condition to the 3/8" wall tile. Set A's main faults are one misread (treating the grid line "E" as a slope direction), a duplicated slope and duplicated wall-tile/PT1 facts, and vague entities ("drawing", "surface"). Both sets miss the 1/2" gypsum wallboard, 3/4" MDF gable w/ P3, steel L-bracket attachment and blocking.
remarks: The text layer flattens the D3 and D5 callouts into one run, so the single "3/8\" PORCELAIN WALL TILE" and "EDGE STRIP" strings each serve two details; attributions to a specific detail cannot be verified from the text layer alone (the image does show the wall tile in both D3 and D5). "PT1" is a finish/paint code, not a substrate or a named surface; both sets handle it poorly (A vaguely as "surface", B misbound as "PT1 substrate"). Facts neither set picks up: 1/2" GYPSUM WALLBOARD, 3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3, STEEL L-BRACKET ATTACHMENT, BLOCKING AS REQ'D, and the "IN BRICK LAYOUT" tile layout.
